name: Travertine
desc: Warm banded stone the water is still building — folded calcite bedding runs cream through buff and ochre to rust, vug cavities open along the porous layers where the dissolution front passes, hard beds stand proud of soft ones under a slow raking light, and thin films of spring water creep down the face, darkening the stone and igniting the wet facets.

energy.doc: relief depth of the bedding and the vugs under the raking light, plus wet-facet sheen

density.doc: number of beds (9-25) and how freely the vug cavities open

hue.doc: base stone hue — 34 is the warm cream/ochre travertine; the cream-to-rust ramp is offset from it

speed.doc: rate of the water films and the wet/dry cycle

scale.doc: size of the fold structure and the vugs — from a hand sample to a quarry face

x.doc: unused anchor, kept for the universal seven

y.doc: unused anchor, kept for the universal seven

tilt.doc: structural dip of the bedding across the frame — 0.5 is horizontal, either extreme tilts the strata

act.doc: cycle: the water films come and go · flood: the face runs wet and saturated · dry: bone dry, chalky, maximum relief contrast

style.doc: travertine: warm porous banded stone under a raking lamp · onyx: translucent alabaster lit by TRANSMISSION through the bedding rather than by surface normal · survey: the schematic — lithological ornament ruled per layer on buff paper · rust: iron-oxide saturated, oxblood and dark ochre

seed.doc: deterministic seed — same number, same stone
